question.text: Which of the following BEST describes the ESSENTIAL characteristic that distinguishes alternative investments from traditional investments per NISM Chapter 2?

answer.text: Alternative investments are always unregulated while traditional investments are SEBI-regulated.

The essential characteristic of alternative investments is 'illiquidity' — they are not readily convertible into cash either because they are off-market or have complex structures without a ready market.
Alternative investments always carry lower risk than traditional investments due to diversification.
Alternative investments can only be held by foreign investors while traditional investments are for domestic investors.

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Chapter 2.1, '[t]he essential characteristic of alternative investments is illiquidity, i.e. they are not readily convertible into cash as they are either off-market investments or because they are complex structures that do not have a ready market.' Traditional investments by contrast are primarily on-market opportunities with liquidity via exchanges or open-ended redemption. The Trap: Option A is false — AIFs and PE are SEBI-regulated under the AIF Regulations 2012. Option B inverts reality — alternatives typically carry HIGHER individual risk, not lower. Option D is fabricated. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-A/B distributor exams define the category from a suitability angle; XXI-B (PM) tests this from a listed-vs-unlisted asset-allocation angle. Manager's Pro-Tip: Build your illiquidity premium argument into every LP pitch. A liquid bond at 8% and an unlisted credit at 12% is not 4% alpha — it is 4% compensation for LP lockup. LPs that don't understand this are LPs that redeem at the worst time.
